nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-01.title: Express the radius
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-01.body:
From $2\pi r=a\pi$, $r=\frac a2$. Then the area is $\pi r^2=\frac{a^2}{4}\pi=4a\pi$, so $a^2=16a$ and, since $a>0$, $a=16$.

**Answer: 16**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-01.title: Ratio of area to circumference
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-01.body:
$\frac{\text{area}}{\text{circumference}}=\frac{\pi r^2}{2\pi r}=\frac r2$, and here it equals $\frac{4a\pi}{a\pi}=4$, so $r=8$. Then $a\pi=2\pi\cdot8$ gives $a=16$.

**Answer: 16**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-02.title: Venn diagram
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-02.body:
Fill in the regions:
- all three: $5$; French and Spanish only: $9-5=4$; French and Italian only: $12-5=7$; French only: $0$.
- Let $x$ speak only Spanish. Spanish total $18$ gives Spanish and Italian only $=18-5-4-x=9-x$.
- Italian total $20$ gives Italian only $=20-7-5-(9-x)=x-1$.

All regions sum to $30$: $0+7+5+4+(x-1)+(9-x)+x=24+x=30$, so $x=6$.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-02.title: Count who is not Italian
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-02.body:
$20$ people speak Italian. Among the other $10$, those who speak French and Spanish but not Italian number $9-5=4$. Everyone else who does not speak Italian speaks exactly one language, French or Spanish, and nobody speaks only French. So $10-4=6$ speak only Spanish.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-03.title: Isosceles right triangle
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-03.body:
Let $AB=x$. Triangle $ABD$ has a right angle at $A$ and $\angle ABD=45^\circ$, so it is isosceles: $AD=x$. The parallel sides are $AB=x$ and $CD=x+6$, with height $AD=x$:
$$\tfrac12\,x\,(2x+6)=88\ \Rightarrow\ x^2+3x-88=0\ \Rightarrow\ (x+11)(x-8)=0.$$
So $x=8$.

**Answer: 8 inches**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-04.title: Use the exponent equations
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-04.body:
From $3^z=3^{x+1}$, $z=x+1$. From $z^x=(y^2)^x$ with $x$ a positive integer, $z=y^2$ or $z=-y^2$. If $z=-y^2$ then $x=z-1<0$, impossible. So $z=y^2$ and $x=y^2-1$. The first equation becomes
$$y^2-1+y+y^2=9\ \Rightarrow\ 2y^2+y-10=0\ \Rightarrow\ (2y+5)(y-2)=0.$$
$y$ is an integer, so $y=2$, $z=4$, $x=3$. Check: $3+2+4=9$, $4^3=64=2^6$, $3^4=3\cdot3^3$.

**Answer: $(3,2,4)$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-05.title: Square the sum
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-05.body:
Let $N$ be the sum, $N>0$. Then
$$N^2=\left(\tfrac74+\sqrt3\right)+\left(\tfrac74-\sqrt3\right)+2\sqrt{\tfrac{49}{16}-3}=\tfrac72+2\cdot\tfrac14=4,$$
so $N=2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-05.title: Denest the radicals
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-05.body:
$\frac74\pm\sqrt3=\left(1\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2$, because $\left(1\pm\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)^2=1+\frac34\pm\sqrt3$. Both $1\pm\frac{\sqrt3}2$ are positive, so the sum is $\left(1+\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)+\left(1-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-07.title: Expand the cube
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-07.body:
With edge $s$: $(s+1)^3-s^3=3s^2+3s+1=217$, so $s^2+s-72=0=(s+9)(s-8)$ and $s=8$. (The volume increase is $217$ cubic inches: $729-512=217$.)

**Answer: 8 inches**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-08.title: Work backwards
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-08.body:
Undo each toss from the end: undoing tails adds $24$, undoing heads halves.
$$0\xrightarrow{T}24\xrightarrow{H}12\xrightarrow{T}36\xrightarrow{H}18\xrightarrow{T}42\xrightarrow{H}21.$$

**Answer: \$21**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-08.title: Algebra forwards
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-08.body:
Starting with $m$: after H, T it is $2m-24$; after H, T again $4m-72$; after H, T again $8m-168$. Setting $8m-168=0$ gives $m=21$.

**Answer: \$21**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-09.title: Angle chase
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-09.body:
Each trisector of the right angle $ABC$ makes $30^\circ$, so $\angle ABE=30^\circ$ and, in right triangle $ABE$, $\angle AEB=60^\circ$. Then $\angle AEG=\angle GEH=\angle HEB=20^\circ$. Points $G$ and $H$ lie on diagonal $AC$, and $\angle EAC=45^\circ$.
- In $\triangle AEG$: $\angle AGE=180^\circ-45^\circ-20^\circ=115^\circ$, so $\angle EGH=180^\circ-115^\circ=65^\circ$.
- In $\triangle AEH$: $\angle AHE=180^\circ-45^\circ-40^\circ=95^\circ$, which is $\angle EHG$.

Ratio: $\frac{65}{95}=\frac{13}{19}$. (Check: $65^\circ+95^\circ+20^\circ=180^\circ$ in $\triangle EGH$.)

**Answer: $\frac{13}{19}$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-10.title: Set up the digit equation
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-10.body:
$81A+9B+C=49C+7B+A$ simplifies to $80A+2B=48C$, i.e. $40A+B=24C$. All digits are base-7 digits ($0$–$6$), and $A,C\ge1$.

$B=24C-40A$ must be a multiple of $8$ in $[0,6]$, so $B=0$ and $5A=3C$, giving $A=3$, $C=5$.

The number is $305_9=243+5=248$, and $503_7=245+3=248$.

**Answer: 248**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-11.title: Coordinates
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-11.body:
$A=(8,0)$, $B=(0,4)$. $C$ is $\frac34$ of the way from $B$ to $A$: $C=(6,1)$. Line $AB$ has slope $-\frac12$, so the perpendicular has slope $2$: $y-1=2(x-6)$. At $y=0$, $x=\frac{11}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}{2}$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-11.title: Similar triangles
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-11.body:
Let $P=(t,0)$. Triangle $ACP$ is right-angled at $C$ and similar to triangle $AOB$ (they share angle $A$). $AB=\sqrt{80}=4\sqrt5$ and $AC=\frac14AB=\sqrt5$. Then $\frac{AP}{AC}=\frac{AB}{AO}$, so $AP=\sqrt5\cdot\frac{4\sqrt5}{8}=\frac52$ and $t=8-\frac52=\frac{11}2$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}{2}$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-12.title: Expand
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-12.body:
$\frac{\sqrt3}2\cos x+\frac12\sin x=2\sin x$ gives $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos x=\frac32\sin x$, so $\tan x=\frac1{\sqrt3}$ ($\cos x=0$ is not a solution). Then $x=30^\circ$ or $210^\circ$, with sum $240^\circ$.

**Answer: 240**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-14.title: Complete the square
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-14.body:
$(x-3)^2+(y+6)^2=25$, so the center is $(3,-6)$. Setting $x=0$: $y^2+12y+20=0$, $y=-2$ or $-10$. The base on the $y$-axis has length $8$ and the height is the distance $3$ from the center to the $y$-axis. Area $=\frac12\cdot8\cdot3=12$.

**Answer: 12**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-15.title: Two cases
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-15.body:
$|x+2|=2|x-2|$ means $x+2=2(x-2)$ or $x+2=-2(x-2)$. The first gives $x=6$; the second gives $3x=2$, $x=\frac23$. Both check.

**Answer: $x=\frac23$ or $x=6$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-16.title: List the candidates
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-16.body:
$X$ and $Y$ must be multiples of $21$ that divide $462=21\cdot22=2\cdot3\cdot7\cdot11$. These are $21,42,231,462$; excluding $21$ leaves $42,231,462$. Every pair from these works: the gcd with $21$ is $21$, and the lcm is $462$ for $(42,231)$, $(42,462)$, $(231,462)$. So there are $3$ pairs.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-18.title: Side in terms of radius
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-18.body:
Let the radius be $r$. Along a side, the two bottom circles touch the side at points $2r$ apart; from each vertex to the nearest tangency point is $r\cot30^\circ=r\sqrt3$ (the circle is inscribed in the $60^\circ$ angle). So the side is $s=2r+2\sqrt3\,r$. The area is
$$\tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2=\sqrt3\,r^2(1+\sqrt3)^2=r^2(6+4\sqrt3).$$
Setting $r^2(6+4\sqrt3)=96+64\sqrt3=16(6+4\sqrt3)$ gives $r^2=16$, so each circle has area $16\pi$.

**Answer: $16\pi$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-20.title: Use perimeter 12
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-20.body:
Take perimeter $12$: the square has side $3$ and circumradius $\frac{3\sqrt2}2$, so $R_A^2=\frac92$. The triangle has side $4$ and circumradius $\frac4{\sqrt3}$, so $R_B^2=\frac{16}3$. The ratio of areas is $\frac{9/2}{16/3}=\frac{27}{32}$.

**Answer: $\frac{27}{32}$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-22.title: Side and diagonal
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-22.body:
Let the side be $s$. The octagon is a square of side $s(1+\sqrt2)$ minus four corner triangles of area $\frac{s^2}4$, so its area is $s^2(1+\sqrt2)^2-s^2=2s^2(1+\sqrt2)$. The rectangle $ABEF$ has sides $AB=s$ and $BE=s(1+\sqrt2)$ (the width of the octagon), so its area is $s^2(1+\sqrt2)$, exactly half the octagon. Hence it is $4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-22.title: Central triangles
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-22.body:
Let $O$ be the center and $R$ the circumradius. The octagon is made of $8$ congruent triangles like $OAB$, each with area $\frac12R^2\sin45^\circ=1$. The diagonals $AE$ and $BF$ of the rectangle are diameters through $O$, so $ABEF$ splits into $OAB$, $OBE$, $OEF$, $OFA$. Here $\angle AOB=\angle EOF=45^\circ$ and $\angle BOE=\angle FOA=135^\circ$, and since $\sin135^\circ=\sin45^\circ$, each of the four triangles has area $\frac12R^2\sin45^\circ=1$. So $[ABEF]=4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-23.title: Difference of times
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-23.body:
The two travel times differ by $2$ minutes $=\frac1{30}$ hour: $\frac d{40}-\frac d{45}=\frac{d}{360}=\frac1{30}$, so $d=12$.

**Answer: 12 miles**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-27.title: Diameter and intersecting chords
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-27.body:
$\angle ADB=90^\circ$ is inscribed, so $AB$ is a diameter. $DE=CD-CE=10$. By intersecting chords, $AE\cdot EB=DE\cdot EC$: $5\cdot EB=80$, so $EB=16$ and $AB=21$. The circumference is $21\pi$.

**Answer: $21\pi$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-28.title: Vieta
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-28.body:
$r+s=5$, $rs=9$. The new roots have sum $(r+s)+\frac{r+s}{rs}=5+\frac59=\frac{50}9$ and product $rs+2+\frac1{rs}=9+2+\frac19=\frac{100}9$. So the equation is $x^2-\frac{50}9x+\frac{100}9=0$, i.e. $9x^2-50x+100=0$, with $\gcd(9,50,100)=1$.

**Answer: $(9,50,100)$**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-29.title: Count the leg lengths
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-29.body:
Let the equal sides be $a$ and the base $b=111-2a\ge1$, so $a\le55$. The triangle inequality $b<2a$ gives $111<4a$, so $a\ge28$. Each $a=28,\dots,55$ gives one triangle (including the equilateral $37,37,37$, counted once), so there are $28$.

**Answer: 28**

nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-30.title: Choose the digit sets
nyciml-2010-11-fall-seniorb-30.body:
Any set of three distinct digits can be arranged in exactly one increasing and one decreasing order.
- Increasing: the leading digit is the smallest, so $0$ cannot be used: $\binom93=84$.
- Decreasing: $0$ can only be last, which is allowed: $\binom{10}3=120$.

Total $84+120=204$.

**Answer: 204**
